result.topic_en: Euler finds the most general expression Z depending on x, y and p satisfying pZ = (1+pp)P, obtaining Z = V√(1+pp), so the integral formula becomes ∫V dx √(1+pp), which he begins to interpret as the time for a body to traverse a curve AM.
result.transcription:
VARIATIONVM TRACTANDI. 61

43. Non igitur pigebit in talem expreſſionem $Z$ inquiſiuiſſe, ac primo quidem patet eam praeter coordinatas $x$ et $y$ etiam quantitatem $p$ inuoluere debere. Sumamus autem praeterea in $Z$ non ingredi litteras $q$, $r$ etc. ita vt ſit $Q=0$, $R=0$, ac noſtra aequatio reſoluenda erit:
$$pZ=(1+pp)P,$$
vbi notandum eſt eſſe
$$dZ=M\,dx+N\,dy+P\,dp,$$
quare ſi ambae coordinatae $x$ et $y$ tanquam conſtantes tractentur erit
$$dZ=P\,dp \quad \text{ideoque} \quad P=\frac{dZ}{dp},$$
quo valore ibi introducto haec prodibit aequatio
$$\frac{dZ}{Z}=\frac{p\,dp}{1+pp}$$
quae integrata dat
$$L.Z=L.\surd(1+pp)+L.C$$
quae conſtans functio quaecunque ipſarum $x$ et $y$ eſſe poteſt, talis functio ſit $V$ atque habebimus
$$Z=V\surd(1+pp),$$
ideoque formula integralis
$$=\int V\,dx\surd(1+pp).$$
Huius formulae ſignificatum ſatis eleganter per tempus, quo corpus quodpiam per curuam $AM$ promouetur exprimi poteſt. Si enim celeritas in puncto $M$, fuerit $=\frac{1}{V}$, hoc eſt ſi celeritas in ſingulis
H 3 punctis

items.quote: Non igitur pigebit in talem expreſſionem $Z$ inquiſiuiſſe
items.english: It will therefore not be irksome to have inquired into such an expression Z.

items.quote: ac primo quidem patet eam praeter coordinatas $x$ et $y$ etiam quantitatem $p$ inuoluere debere
items.english: And first indeed it is clear that it must involve, besides the coordinates x and y, also the quantity p.

items.quote: Huius formulae ſignificatum ſatis eleganter per tempus, quo corpus quodpiam per curuam $AM$ promouetur exprimi poteſt.
items.english: The meaning of this formula can be expressed quite elegantly by the time in which some body is moved along the curve AM.
